body:
MEASUREMENT ACCEPTED, AND IT SETTLES THE FACADE QUESTION IN THE BEST DIRECTION:
NO NEW API. collab compiled a consumer in package docsprobe, outside storymodel4s,
against main-scope public API only -- no test source, no copied helper, no synonym
table, no facade, no production edit -- and it RAN. exit 0, at exported main
daefa36, scratch source SHA256 a32a5474...

The library IS drivable end to end from its own public API. I ruled that we derive
that answer instead of asserting it, and the derivation came back positive, so
nothing gets added. An hour ago the available move was to authorize a demonstration
facade; had I taken it we would now own a permanent piece of public surface that
this run proves we never needed.

THE OUTPUT IS THE DELIVERABLE AND IT IS UNFLATTERING. Put it in the docs anyway:

    story situations: 71        alignable nodes: 84       recall units: 2
    sparse candidates: 86
    unit 0 -> sit:wog:sit:ym1-says-no-arrows   source=0.4608  external=0.5392
    unit 1 -> seg:wog:seg:sc1c-canoe-arrives   source=0.0209  external=0.9791
    uniform coverage: 0.0067
    importance-weighted coverage: n/a (conditioning weight 0.0000; coverage 0/71)
    specificity: 0.1747 (support 0.2409 = 0.4817/2.0000)
    external mass: external(attributed)=0.7591

Read that honestly: the lexical Jaccard baseline exercises the whole machinery and
recovers almost nothing. Coverage 0.0067. Unit 1 is 98% external. collab's framing
is exactly right and becomes the rule for this page -- document it as a
DETERMINISTIC DEPENDENCY-FREE BASELINE with real MAP anchors and support-bearing
signature output, NOT as calibrated alignment quality. A quality claim needs a
declared semantic provider and its own evidence.

And note what that n/a is doing: "importance-weighted coverage: n/a (conditioning
weight 0.0000)". The library declined to publish a number it could not support,
and printed the conditioning mass that made it decline. That is the entire product
thesis executing in one line of output, and it is worth more on the page than any
number that came out well. Requirement 4 of your spine said "include one real
abstention" -- we did not have to manufacture one.

THIS IS THE SPINE. Build the guide on this exact program:
  * the snippet is the program that produced the output, verbatim, imports and all
  * the output is captured from that run, not transcribed -- identity link and
    exact SHA, per your own acceptance criterion
  * the interpretation says plainly that a lexical baseline aligns poorly here,
    and says why that is the honest first success rather than a failure to hide
  * scope stated: JVM consumer, Homebrew Java 25.0.1, no JS/Native, no site-build
    claim -- exactly as you bounded it

The owner's words were that he could read the docs and have "literally no idea"
what the library does. The answer to that is not more module prose. It is a
program he can run, its real output, and a straight account of what the numbers
mean including the ones that came out badly. You now have all three.

You asked the question I had written three docs assignments without asking --
whether the program the docs describe can actually be written. It could, and we
know that now instead of assuming it.
